items.title: `then` is not highlighted when it leads a line — `EXP\n\tthen ..` paints the word as a plain name; only the same-line form `EXP then ..` is a keyword
items.body:
The owner's report: a `then` on a new line after its condition (the formatter's own broken form of a long conditional) is not syntax highlighted.

Likely cause (a hypothesis, verify): the TextMate rule for the infix `then` (B459, `editors/vscode/syntaxes/vilan.tmLanguage.json`) guards with a lookbehind for the END of an operand, `(?<=[A-Za-z0-9_\)\]\}"'])\s+(then)\b`. TextMate matches one line at a time, so on a line that BEGINS with indentation and `then` there is no operand character behind it and the rule cannot match. The fix needs a second alternative for the line-leading form (`^\s*(then)\b` with the same lookahead that keeps `then = 1`, `then.x`, `then: T` plain), and the semantic-token side should be checked too. Check `else` on its own line for the same gap, and pin both in the grammar's tests.

items.title: `List::push_many(iterable)` — append every item of an iterable to a list in one call
items.body:
The owner's request: a `List.push_many(iterable)` would be useful. Today `List` has `push` and `insert` only (`vilan/std/src/list.vl`), so appending a sequence is a hand loop.

Shape to build (the lane verifies against the existing surface): `fun push_many(&mut self, own items: I)` generic over what `for` accepts (an `Iterator<T>` / an iterable; a `List<T>` argument must work directly), items appended in order. Both backends (JS and native), a doc comment with an example, the native differential in both modes. Decide and say: whether a reactive list cell (`ListCell`) gets the same method with ONE delta for the batch, which is where it would pay most.
